questions.question: List the optical parts of a compound microscope.
questions.solution_html:
• Optical parts of microscope
  • o Eyepiece (ocular lens), objective lenses, condenser, mirror/light source

questions.solution_html:

  • o Liquid (broth), semi-solid, solid

  • o Organisms that synthesize their own food using CO₂ as carbon source

• Structure for bacterial motility
  • o Flagella

questions.question: Define biosynthesis in viral replication
questions.solution_html:
• Biosynthesis in viral replication
  • o Synthesis of viral nucleic acid and proteins inside host cell

questions.question: Define eukaryotes
questions.solution_html:
• Eukaryotes
  • o Organisms with true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles

questions.question: Define the term microbial nutrition of bacteria.
questions.solution_html:
• Microbial nutrition
  • o Process by which microorganisms obtain nutrients for growth and metabolism

questions.question: Identify the common foods associated with Ochratoxin A
questions.solution_html:
• Foods associated with Ochratoxin A
  • o Cereals, coffee, dried fruits, spices

questions.question: Identify the organisms that cause "surface slime" in meat.
questions.solution_html:
• Organisms causing surface slime in meat
  • o Pseudomonas spp., Achromobacter
questions.final_answer: Organisms causing surface slime in meat

questions.question: Define microbial spoilage of food
questions.solution_html:
• Microbial spoilage of food
  • • Undesirable changes in food caused by microbial activity

questions.question: Define the term Flipper
questions.solution_html:
• Flipper
  • o A flipper can is a type of spoiled can in which both ends appear normal (flat), but
  • when one end is pressed, the other end bulges or flips out.
questions.final_answer: when one end is pressed, the other end bulges or flips out

  • o Bluish discoloration due to Pseudomonas syncyanea

questions.question: Describe dry heat sterilization briefly.
questions.solution_html:
• Dry heat sterilization ((5 marks))
  • • Definition (1)
  • • Principle: oxidation of cell components (1)
  • • Methods: Flaming , hot air oven , incineration(1)
  • • Conditions: 160–180°C for 2 hrs (1)
  • • Applications: glassware, powders, oils (1)

questions.question: Name the components of anaerobic jar and briefly explain each / component.
questions.solution_html:
• Anaerobic jar components ((5 marks))
  • • Jar container (1)
  • • Gas pack (H₂ + CO₂ generation) (1)
  • • Catalyst (palladium) (1)
  • • Indicator (methylene blue/resazurin) (1)
  • • Function explanation (removal of O₂) (1)

questions.question: Define Listeriosis including risk group, foods involved, symptoms and / control measures.
questions.solution_html:
• Listeriosis ((5 marks))
  • • Causative agent: Listeria monocytogenes (1)
  • • Risk groups: pregnant, elderly, immunocompromised (1)
  • • Foods: milk, cheese, ready-to-eat meat (1)
  • • Symptoms: fever, meningitis, miscarriage (1)
  • • Prevention: pasteurization, hygiene (1)

questions.question: Define food poisoning . Explain its common sources and symptoms.
questions.solution_html:
• Food poisoning ((5 marks))
  • • Definition (1)
  • • Sources: contaminated food/water (1)
  • • Causes: bacteria/toxins (1)
  • • Symptoms: vomiting, diarrhea, fever (1)
  • • Prevention: hygiene, proper cooking (1)

questions.question: Define Giardiasis and briefly explain the causative agent, common / foods involved, clinical symptoms, and preventive measures of giardiasis.
questions.solution_html:
• Giardiasis ((5 marks))
  • • Agent: Giardia lamblia (1)
  • • Transmission: contaminated water/food (1)
  • • Foods: raw vegetables, water (1)
  • • Symptoms: diarrhea, bloating (1)
  • • Prevention: sanitation, safe water (1)

questions.question: List out the bacterial spoilage occuring in fish
questions.solution_html:
• Bacterial spoilage in fish ((5 marks))
  • • Surface slime (1)
  • • Off-odour (trimethylamine) (1)
  • • Discoloration (1)
  • • Softening of tissue, Autolysis (1)
  • • Gas production (1)

questions.question: Classify fungi based on morphology and mode of reproduction with / suitable examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Classification of fungi ((10 marks))
  • • Introduction (1)
  • • Based on morphology (3)
  • o Yeasts, Yeast like, molds, dimorphic fungi
  • • Based on reproduction (4)
  • o Asexual: spores
  • o Sexual: zygospores, ascospores, basidiospores

questions.question: Explain Botulism with its causative organism, source of contamination, / foods involved , incubation period , toxin formation, symptoms and preventive measures.
questions.solution_html:
• Botulism ((10 marks))
  • • Causative organism: Clostridium botulinum (1)
  • • Source: soil, canned foods (2)
  • • Foods involved (1)
  • • Incubation period (1)
  • • Toxin production (1)
  • • Types: Adult botulism and Infant botulism (1)
  • • Symptoms: paralysis, respiratory failure, blurred vision (2)
  • • Prevention: proper canning, heating (1)

questions.question: Explain the major types of spoilage in fruits and vegetables during post- / harvest storage
questions.solution_html:
• Spoilage of fruits & vegetables ((10 marks))
  • • Introduction (1)
  • • Types of spoilage (5)
  • o Fungal rot
  • o Bacterial soft rot -Erwinia carotovora
  • o Gray mold rot- Botrytis cineria
  • o Rhizopus soft rot- Rhizopus stolonifer
  • o Anthracnose- Colletotrichum lindemuthianum
  • o Alternaria rot- Alternaria tenuis
  • o Blue mold rot – Penicillium digitatum
  • o Downey mildew- Phytophthora
  • o Watery soft rot- Sclerotinia sclerotiorum
  • o Stem end rots- Alternaria, fusarium
  • o Black mold rot – Alternaria
  • o Pink mold rot- Trichothecium roseum
  • o Green mold rot- Cladosporium, Trichoderma
  • o Brown rot-Sclerotinia
  • o Yeast fermentation
  • • Causes (2)
  • o Enzymatic browning
  • o Physical damage
  • o Microbial
  • • Prevention methods (2)
